must_haves: Adults, at least a few thousand participants with device data (read as roughly 3,000 or more)
Wrist-worn accelerometer or activity tracker worn in free-living daily life
Wear duration of several days to a week or longer
Linked follow-up outcomes: hospital records, diagnoses or death registrations
Obtainable by a US university researcher through an application process (applications acceptable)

A.access_stated: Register on AMS, project application, institution signs MTA and pays fee, analysis on the Research Analysis Platform only; about weeks
A.note: The route described (AMS application, MTA, fee, RAP-only analysis) matches the official process, but it is not open now. Direct fetches of ukbiobank.ac.uk and community.ukbiobank.ac.uk returned 403 more than twice, so access text comes from search-indexed official pages, which state "Applications are currently paused whilst necessary changes are made to the UK Biobank Research Analysis Platform" and "UKB-RAP is currently closed whilst we implement necessary changes" (latest dated evidence: community FAQ updated 22 October 2026, aiming to reopen applications in late 2026), so an application with approval in weeks is not available today; the device facts (Axivity AX3, dominant wrist, seven days, 103,720 participants 2013-2015) are confirmed in the UK Biobank Physical Activity Monitor document (biobank.ctsu.ox.ac.uk/ukb/ukb/docs/PhysicalActivityMonitor.pdf).

A.dataset: NHANES 2011-2014 wrist accelerometer + NCHS linked mortality files
A.access_stated: Public download with no account; public-use linked mortality files; restricted-use files only via NCHS RDC application
A.note: The NCHS page links the public-use LMFs on a public FTP directory ("a limited set of mortality (death) data for adults") and states "Restricted-use LMFs can be accessed only through the NCHS Research Data Center (RDC) network for approved projects"; the PAXDAY_G documentation confirms an ActiGraph GT3X+ worn on the non-dominant wrist "all day and night for seven full days" (6,917 participants aged 6+ in 2011-2012, 7,776 in 2013-2014).

A.access_stated: Registered Tier with a data passport in the Researcher Workbench; institutional agreement and training (the last two from memory)
A.note: The register page states "Only researchers whose institutions have signed a DURA may access the Researcher Workbench" and requires identity verification and Responsible Conduct of Research training, and the data-access page says "Authorized users will receive a 'data passport'" with the Registered Tier including EHR and wearables data; the Fitbit participant count (more than 59,000) comes from a 2026 Nature Medicine paper, not the owner's page.

A.access_stated: Free sleepdata.org account, then a data use agreement per dataset; approval in days
A.note: sleepdata.org failed twice with an SSL certificate error, so NSRR's official documentation repository on GitHub (the source of the sleepdata.org dataset pages) was read instead; it states "The MrOS dataset on NSRR is limited in scope (e.g. no actigraphy raw data or results are included)" and points to MrOS Online (account plus a Data Use Agreement) for other data, so the actigraphy and outcomes are not obtained through an NSRR request; the study itself fits (3,135 men with 3 to 5-day actigraphy, mortality and fracture objectives), with wrist placement (non-dominant, SleepWatch-O) taken from published MrOS papers.

A.access_stated: Free sleepdata.org account, then a data use agreement per dataset; approval in days
A.note: sleepdata.org failed twice with an SSL certificate error, so NSRR's official documentation repository on GitHub (the source of the sleepdata.org dataset pages) was read instead; the NSRR SOF release is polysomnography only ("Sleep studies were completed on 461 SOF participants at Visit 8", "The dataset contains 461 records", no actigraphy variables in the NSRR data dictionary), so the Visit 8 actigraphy comes from SOF Online (account plus a Data Use Agreement); the SOF Online Study Overview reports follow-up above 98% for vital status, and the wrist actigraphy count (about 3,127 women, non-dominant wrist) comes from published SOF papers.

A.access_stated: Free sleepdata.org account, then a data use agreement per dataset; approval in days
A.note: sleepdata.org failed twice with an SSL certificate error, so NSRR's official documentation repository on GitHub (the source of the sleepdata.org dataset pages) was read instead, which confirms NSRR hosts "7-day wrist-worn actigraphy" for MESA Sleep, and search-indexed sleepdata.org text states "the NSRR provides all data cost-free to incoming users who complete an online data request" under a web-based Data Access and Use Agreement; however only 2,237 participants were enrolled (2,159 with epoch files), below "at least a few thousand", and outcome data come from other MESA exams via BioLINCC or the MESA Coordinating Center, not the NSRR release.

The page states "Anyone can access the files, as long as they conform to the terms of the specified license" (CC0 1.0) and covers 14,693 NHANES 2011-2014 participants who "wore an ActiGraph GT3X+ on the non-dominant wrist for seven consecutive days"; it carries no outcome variables itself, but every file includes the NHANES ID SEQN, so it links to the public-use NCHS mortality files exactly as the NHANES files do.

UCL pages returned 403 on two direct fetches; search-indexed UCL text states "All proposals are reviewed by the data sharing committee" and that approved applicants "sign the WII Data Sharing Agreement ... and proceed with the payment" (GBP 500 + VAT, or free via DPUK, lead time 1-2 months on HDR UK Gateway), consistent with the answer; a 2017 Whitehall II paper reports 3,749 participants with a wrist accelerometer worn for 9 days, but linkage to hospital or mortality records could not be confirmed on an official page.

A.access_stated: Application; months; unsure whether accelerometer data are released
A.note: ckbiobank.org returned 403 on two direct fetches and no search-indexed access text was found, so access and data release could not be established; the accelerometer study exists (a 2023 IJBNPA paper reports 22,511 3rd-resurvey participants who agreed to wear an Axivity AX3 wrist accelerometer for seven days in 2020-2021).

B.access_stated: By application; confirm sample size and international access terms
B.note: ckbiobank.org returned 403 on two direct fetches and no search-indexed access text was found, so access and data release could not be established; the accelerometer study exists (a 2023 IJBNPA paper reports 22,511 3rd-resurvey participants who agreed to wear an Axivity AX3 wrist accelerometer for seven days in 2020-2021).
